stories.title: Blue Owl Preps $513M CMBS Data Center Deal
stories.excerpt: The mounting political headwinds confronting data centers are not slowing the sector’s presence in the capital markets. Blue Owl Capital is slated to access the single-asset, single-borrower (SASB) commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) market with a $513 million deal to finance the acquisition of a newly constructed data center in Northern Virginia fully leased to Amazon, Bloomberg reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the transaction. The SASB loan is securitized by the 54-megawatt Project Crossing III data center project in Gainesville, Va., where Amazon has a long-term lease that runs through 2042 with two five-year renewal options, according to Bloomberg. The property encompasses the third data center in the Gainesville Crossing Data Center campus that will eventually feature five facilities with 326 megawatts. The Gainesville Crossing campus was developed by Corscale Data Centers and Affinius Capital, which secured a $975 million loan from Blue Owl in June to recapitalize the newly built data center, Commercial Observer reported at the time. The property is in Loudon County, which on Tuesday adopted a 12-month moratorium on new data centers after the area became home to the largest concentration of data centers in the world through large-scale developments over the last decade. News of the CMBS deal was reported hours before Michael Lascher, head of capital markets and asset management at Blue Owl, spoke at New York University Schack Institute of Real Estate Capital Markets conference Wednesday about continued market appetite for the sector despite recent political and community opposition to the projects. He said hyperscalers demand remains high for data centers and the extra hurdles will position Blue Owl well, given its vast experience. “What it does do is make what is already built more valuable because there are higher barriers to building more,” said Lascher during the NYU conference’s global finance and capital markets panel held at the P
bullets: Blue Owl securitizes $513M SASB CMBS for Amazon-leased data center in Gainesville, Virginia.
Project Crossing III is 54-megawatt facility with long-term Amazon lease through 2042 plus renewals.
Campus will eventually total 326 megawatts across five facilities; Blue Owl provided $975M recapitalization in June.
stories.summary: Blue Owl Capital is financing the acquisition of a newly constructed, fully leased data center in Northern Virginia through a $513 million single-asset CMBS deal. The Project Crossing III facility in Gainesville is a 54-megawatt data center with an Amazon long-term lease running through 2042 and two five-year renewal options. It is the third of five planned facilities on the Gainesville Crossing campus, which will ultimately reach 326 megawatts of capacity developed by Corscale Data Centers and Affinius Capital.
stories.impact: Data center financing remains robust despite political headwinds, signaling continued capital availability for specialized real estate. However, this has minimal direct impact on multifamily development; the strong CMBS market for non-residential assets may compete for capital allocation but does not materially affect residential demand, supply, or underwriting in core multifamily markets.

stories.title: Centennial Bank Lends $51M to Expand Miami-Dade Nursing Home
stories.excerpt: Abraham Shaulson’s Millennium Management and Manuel Scharf have secured a $51.2 million construction loan to expand a nursing home in Miami-Dade County. The financing from Centennial Bank covers the Terraces of Hialeah, a 55,518-square-foot facility at 195 West 27th Street, sandwiched between Red Road and the Hialeah Park Casino. The asset was built on a 2.6-acre site between 1950 and 1967. The redevelopment will increase the property’s footprint to 114,865 square feet and double the number of residential units from 86 to 172, though the number of licensed beds will remain unchanged at 276, according to a representative for the lender. Portions of the existing structure will be demolished to make space for a surface parking lot and a new three-story facility, while the two-story building facing 28th Street will remain. Construction, which is expected to take 18 months, will begin after a 60-day notice period for residents, though about 109 beds will remain operational throughout the redevelopment, per Centennial Bank. Investors are increasingly targeting senior living facilities across South Florida, where the senior population is expected to grow by 2.2 million by 2040, according to state estimates. This month, health care real estate investment trust Welltower has spent over $386 million on nine properties across the region, The Real Deal reported. Other recent transactions include the Artemis Real Estate Partners’ $140 million purchase of a 7.2-acre asset and Fortress Investment Group’s $26 million acquisition of a 118-bed property, both in Delray Beach. The owners of Terraces of Hialeah could not be reached for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Centennial Bank finances $51.2M construction loan for Terraces of Hialeah nursing home expansion in Miami-Dade.
Project doubles residential units from 86 to 172 (276 licensed beds unchanged); expands footprint from 55,518 to 114,865 SF.
18-month construction timeline; about 109 beds remain operational during redevelopment; investors increasingly target South Florida senior living.
stories.summary: Millennium Management and Manuel Scharf secured a $51.2 million construction loan from Centennial Bank to expand the Terraces of Hialeah, a nursing home in Miami-Dade County. The redevelopment will increase the property's square footage from 55,518 SF to 114,865 SF and double residential units from 86 to 172, though licensed bed count remains at 276. Construction is expected to take 18 months, with approximately 109 beds remaining operational throughout.
stories.impact: Senior living capital deployment in South Florida signals demographic tailwinds and investor confidence in that aging-in-place thesis, but does not directly affect multifamily rental demand or supply. However, it underscores the Miami-Dade market's overall appeal to real estate capital and its ability to absorb diverse asset types, which may intensify competition for prime development sites and labor availability for multifamily projects in the region.

stories.title: Sherman Associates Marks First Residential Opening at Beltline Station in St. Louis Park
stories.excerpt: Sherman Associates has opened Solene, a new 146-unit luxury apartment community in St. Louis Park. This marks Sherman Associates’ entry into the City of St. Louis Park and the first residential milestone at Beltline Station, the company’s multi-phase, mixed-use development currently under construction. “With a location adjacent to the Cedar Lake Trail and the soon-to-be-opened METRO Green Line, we’re excited that residents of Solene will benefit from direct, reliable access to regional transit connecting them to opportunities across the metro area,” said Karen Barton, City of St. Louis Park Community Development Director. “We look forward to the remainder of the Beltline Boulevard Station being completed in the coming months.”Located at 3130 Monterey Avenue South, Solene is a five-story community with alcove, one-bedroom, one-bedroom-plus-den, two-bedroom and two-bedroom-plus-den residences. Construction continues across the remaining phases of Beltline Station, with additional residential and commercial spaces opening through 2027. The post Sherman Associates Marks First Residential Opening at Beltline Station in St. Louis Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sherman Associates opens Solene, 146-unit luxury apartment community in St. Louis Park, Minnesota.
First residential phase of mixed-use Beltline Station development; located adjacent to Cedar Lake Trail and future METRO Green Line.
Transit-oriented location connects residents to regional opportunities across Minneapolis metro area.
stories.summary: Sherman Associates has opened Solene, a 146-unit luxury apartment community in St. Louis Park, Minnesota, marking the developer's entry into the suburb and the first residential phase of the Beltline Station mixed-use development. The property is positioned adjacent to the Cedar Lake Trail and the soon-to-open METRO Green Line, providing direct transit access to regional employment centers. The development is part of a larger multi-phase project still under construction.
stories.impact: The opening of Solene and imminent Green Line connection signals strong demand drivers for transit-oriented multifamily in the Minneapolis metro's inner-ring suburbs. This validates the TOD thesis and suggests residents will pay a premium for car-free accessibility to downtown jobs and amenities, creating urgency for competing developers to acquire and entitle transit-adjacent infill sites before major transit opens.

stories.title: Keystone Group Acquires 30-Story BMO Tower in Indiana
stories.excerpt: Keystone Group announced the acquisition of BMO Tower, a prominent 30-story office tower and the sixth-tallest building in Indiana, located at 135 N. Pennsylvania St., just one block from Monument Circle in downtown Indianapolis. The acquisition marks the ninth property in Keystone’s current downtown Indianapolis portfolio and advances a long-term vision for downtown that Keystone has been executing since 2002. “With our growing portfolio of landmark properties within blocks of Monument Circle, now is the right time to bring BMO Tower into the fold,” said Ersal Ozdemir, Founder and Owner of Keystone Group. “We’re building on a generational opportunity to revitalize Monument Circle and its surrounding district through transformative development, creating a complete destination to live, work, play and stay.” Completed in 1988, BMO Tower totals approximately 627,000 square feet, including 445,000 square feet of Class A office space, 19,000 square feet of retail space, and an on-site parking garage with 390 spaces. BMO serves as the building’s anchor tenant, and BMO Tower joins a portfolio of developments and redevelopments shaping Keystone Group’s revitalization of Monument Circle. The post Keystone Group Acquires 30-Story BMO Tower in Indiana appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Keystone Group acquires BMO Tower, 30-story office building (627K SF) in downtown Indianapolis.
Building completed 1988; includes 445K SF Class A office, 19K SF retail, 390-space parking garage; BMO is anchor tenant.
Acquisition is Keystone's ninth downtown Indianapolis property; part of generational Monument Circle revitalization vision since 2002.
stories.summary: Keystone Group has acquired BMO Tower, a 30-story office tower at 135 N. Pennsylvania Street in downtown Indianapolis, the sixth-tallest building in Indiana. The 627,000-square-foot property includes 445,000 SF of Class A office, 19,000 SF of retail, and a 390-space parking garage, with BMO serving as anchor tenant. The acquisition marks Keystone's ninth downtown Indianapolis property and advances its long-term revitalization strategy for the Monument Circle district.
stories.impact: Keystone's continued office acquisition in downtown Indianapolis, while focused on mixed-use and placemaking, does not directly drive multifamily demand or supply. However, the firm's consolidation of nine properties around Monument Circle suggests potential for future office-to-residential conversions or ground-floor retail activation that could anchor new multifamily development nearby, particularly if downtown job concentration grows or if conversion economics improve.

stories.title: Sporting Goods Giant Building Castroville Store
stories.excerpt: Academy Sports and Outdoors is planning to build a 55,015-square-foot store in Castroville, near San Antonio. The company will start work next spring and wrap up in October of 2027. The cost of the project is estimated at $6 million. The San Antonio Business Journal reports that Merit Commercial is developing the store in a large retail development called Alsatian Oaks. Alsatian Oaks’ other tenants include Ulta, Ross, Burlington, Marshalls, Five Below, Rack Room Shoes, Bath & Body Works, James Avery and Portillo’s. Academy was founded in 1938 by Max Gochman in San Antonio. It has since moved its corporate office and distribution center to 1800 N. Mason Road in Katy. The sports retailer has eight locations in San Antonio. The company is expanding quickly, opening 15 stores in Q3 and planning to open 23 across 10 states by the end of fiscal 2026. Academy operates more than 300 stores across 21 states. The post Sporting Goods Giant Building Castroville Store appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Academy Sports and Outdoors building 55,015 SF store in Castroville near San Antonio; $6M project.
Construction starts spring 2026, completes October 2027; located in Alsatian Oaks retail development.
Academy expanding rapidly: 15 store openings in Q3; targeting 23 openings across 10 states by end of fiscal 2026.
stories.summary: Academy Sports and Outdoors is building a 55,015-square-foot store in Castroville near San Antonio as part of the Alsatian Oaks retail development, with construction beginning spring 2026 and completing October 2027 at an estimated cost of $6 million. The company is expanding aggressively, having opened 15 stores in Q3 and planning to open 23 stores across 10 states by the end of fiscal 2026. The retailer, founded in San Antonio in 1938, now operates eight locations in the city.
stories.impact: Academy's rapid national expansion signals consumer spending strength in secondary and tertiary markets, which correlates with job growth and in-migration pressures. The Castroville project (outer San Antonio metro) suggests demand-side confidence in suburban and exurban markets; however, this retail-focused news has minimal direct multifamily impact unless anchor retail tenants drive commercial density that attracts residential mixed-use development.

stories.title: MWI Property Group Announces 154K-SF Lease at Palatine Corporate Center
stories.excerpt: MWI Property Group announced a long-term, 153,687-square-foot, full-building lease with ECOS, a pioneering manufacturer of safer, more sustainable laundry detergents and cleaning products, at 150 Sellstrom Drive in Palatine, Illinois, located within its Palatine Corporate Center development. The new Palatine location will accommodate the expansion and relocation of ECOS’s Chicagoland production, packaging, and warehousing operations, retaining 100 employees in the area, with plans to create additional green jobs in the coming year. Palatine Corporate Center is a 25-acre, state-of-the-art industrial redevelopment project comprising two buildings totaling 428,431 square feet. The Class A development offers immediate access to Illinois Route 53 and the I-90 and I-290 interchanges. Sam Durkin and Steve Trapp of JLL represented MWI Property Group on the development and lease transaction. Alex Hayden and Mike Sedjo of CBRE represented ECOS. MWI Construction LLC served as the design-build general contractor and construction manager for both buildings. The company is consolidating and expanding its Chicagoland production, packaging, and warehousing operations, retaining 100 employees with plans to add green jobs. The 25-acre Palatine Corporate Center development comprises two Class A industrial buildings totaling 428,431 square feet with immediate I-90 and I-290 interchange access.
stories.impact: ECOS's relocation and expansion to suburban Chicagoland industrial space signals employer confidence in that market and local labor availability. This job-retention and job-creation activity supports multifamily demand in Chicagoland's northwest suburbs (Palatine-Schaumburg corridor); developers should monitor warehousing and light manufacturing clusters for clustering effects that drive residential demand near employment nodes.

stories.title: JBG Smith Affiliate Leads $52M NoVA Apartment Buy With Amazon Financing
stories.excerpt: JBG Smith subsidiary Leo Impact Capital has led the $51.5 million acquisition of a 176-unit apartment complex in Northern Virginia, with an undisclosed amount of financing from Amazon to preserve long-term housing affordability. Leo Impact Capital and its partners acquired Evermont at Falls Church from Mill Creek Residential for approximately $293,000 per unit. The property is at 2158 Evans Court in Fairfax County’s Pimmit Hills neighborhood. Built in 1966, Evermont consists of eight three-story buildings on approximately 9 acres. The property is 97 percent occupied, with 80 one-bedroom units and 96 two- and three-bedroom apartments. Leo took an equity stake through its Leo Impact Housing Fund, while the Amazon Housing Fund provided subordinate financing. Nonprofit Washington Housing Conservancy (WHC) joined as a minority equity partner and will oversee resident programming. The agreement also creates a pathway for the conservancy to potentially expand its ownership in the future. Under 99-year affordability covenants, at least 60 percent of the apartments will be reserved for households earning no more than 80 percent of the area median income. The restrictions will be phased in as units become available, without displacing existing residents. All apartments were renovated between 2019 and 2023. Amenities include a swimming pool, a fitness center, a playground, a dog park and a resident lounge. The property sits inside the Capital Beltway near Tysons Corner, approximately 10 miles from Amazon’s HQ2 in Arlington. The surrounding neighborhood has a median household income of nearly $170,000 and a median home value exceeding $1 million. Leo’s broader portfolio now includes 12 workforce housing communities totaling more than 3,350 apartments. Meanwhile, the Amazon Housing Fund has committed $3.6 billion to creating and preserving more than 35,000 affordable homes across the Washington, D.C., Puget Sound, Wash., and Nashville regions. The property is subject to 99-year affordability covenants maintaining 60% affordability. Washington Housing Conservancy joined as a minority equity partner and will oversee resident programming, with a pathway to expand ownership over time.
stories.impact: Amazon's continued use of its Housing Fund as subordinate debt on NoVA multifamily reveals the company's strategic interest in securing workforce housing near its Northern Virginia operations and signaling a willingness to subordinate returns for mission alignment. This creates opportunity for multifamily developers: equity sources and Amazon itself may favor affordable preservation deals in Northern Virginia submarkets with strong employment anchors, lowering required returns and opening deal flow otherwise unavailable in a higher-cap-rate environment.

Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of Maverick on Gilmer, a 200-unit multifamily community in Longview, Texas. Nick Fluellen, Bard Hoover, Kevin Parrish and Matt Aslan, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s Dallas office, represented the buyer and seller in the transaction and procured the buyer. NewQuest has secured a 1.18-acre ground lease with Murphy Oil USA Inc. to develop a fueling station and convenience store on the doorstep of Joe V’s Smart Shop in North Houston. stories.title: Actors Federal Credit Union Expands to 15K SF at 1560 Broadway
stories.excerpt: A credit union for performers is expanding its role in Times Square. Actors Federal Credit Union, founded in 1962 to serve members of the entertainment community, signed a 10-year deal to add 4,777 square feet to its existing 10,717-square-foot office footprint at GFP Real Estate’s 1560 Broadway, where it has been headquartered for about 35 years. The deal brings the union’s footprint at the Theatre District building on West 46th Street to 15,494 square feet, according to the landlord. Asking rent was not disclosed, but the average office asking rent in Midtown was $85.53 per square foot in the third quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Actors Federal Credit Union has been part of 1560 Broadway for more than 35 years, and we’ve worked closely with them over that time to accommodate their changing space requirements,” GFP’s Alan Steinberg, who represented the landlord in-house, said in a statement. “This latest expansion allows them to bring their operations and offices together on one floor, while continuing to operate from a building that has been their home for decades.” Joseph Harkins of Cushman & Wakefield negotiated on behalf of the tenant and did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The not-for-profit bank is member-owned, and its last expansion to 10,717 square feet took place in 2023, according to GFP. Other tenants in the building include nonprofit media organization Jewish Education in Media, which signed a five-year renewal for its space spanning 4,385 square feet in June 2025, and technical production company Tinc Productions, which signed a 2,964-square-foot lease in January 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Actors Federal Credit Union expands 10,717 SF to 15,494 SF at 1560 Broadway in Times Square; 10-year lease.
Adds 4,777 SF to existing footprint; consolidates operations on one floor after 35+ years at property.
Midtown office asking rent averaged $85.53/SF in Q3 2026 per CBRE.
stories.summary: Actors Federal Credit Union, founded in 1962 to serve entertainment professionals, has signed a 10-year lease to expand its footprint at 1560 Broadway in Times Square from 10,717 SF to 15,494 SF, adding 4,777 SF. The expansion consolidates operations on a single floor. The lease comes amid Midtown office asking rents averaging $85.53 per square foot in Q3 2026.
stories.impact: This renewal and expansion signals modest stability in niche Midtown office tenancy but reflects continued softness in Manhattan office leasing (rates and tenant consolidation). No direct multifamily impact; however, persistent office weakness and tenant downsizing across Midtown may eventually create conversion opportunities for developers, particularly for older office stock in secondary locations that multifamily could reposition at competitive cost.

stories.title: $250M CMBS Loan Backed by Jersey City’s 101 Hudson Street Sent to Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: A $250 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan secured 101 Hudson Street, a 42-story, 1.4 million-square-foot office building in Jersey City, N.J., to special servicing after missing its October 2026 maturity date, according to an alert from Morningstar Credit. The $250 million loan — which makes up parts of multiple conduits — has been troubled for a while, as the asset’s net cash flow failed to meet its underwriting in the first year of the loan’s origination. Payments have stayed above water due to a debt service coverage ratio that has benefited from the low leverage terms the loan originated under in 2016, per Morningstar. Developed by LCOR, 101 Hudson Street opened in 1992 as the tallest office tower in New Jersey. It became known as the Merrill Lynch Building, as the eponymous bank took up 600,000 square feet as anchor tenant (and had equity interest in the property). A partnership that includes Mark Meisner of the Birch Group and Abe Greenhut of 2020 Vision bought the asset in October 2022 from Veris Residential for $346 million CO reported at the time that SKW provided a $250 million CMBS loan and $78 million in preferred equity. The buyers added an additional $70 million equity investment to fund both the acquisition and stabilization. Even with all this capital, occupancy has declined over the last eight years, falling first to 70 percent once tenant National Union Fire Insurance vacated in 2018, and dropping to 64 percent in recent months, per Morningstar. Merrill Lynch remains the building’s largest tenant with nearly 30 percent of office space, but the company’s lease expires in five months. Birch Group did not respond to requests for comment. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: 101 Hudson Street (42-story, 1.4M SF office tower, Jersey City) $250M CMBS loan sent to special servicing after October 2026 maturity miss.
Asset opened 1992 as tallest NJ office tower; Merrill Lynch was 600K SF anchor tenant; purchased October 2022 for $346M.
Loan troubled since origination; net cash flow underperformed underwriting; DSCR kept above water by low 2016 leverage terms.
stories.summary: A $250 million CMBS loan backed by 101 Hudson Street, a 42-story, 1.4 million-square-foot office tower in Jersey City, has been placed in special servicing after missing its October 2026 maturity date. The property, which opened in 1992 as New Jersey's tallest office building with Merrill Lynch as a 600,000-SF anchor tenant, was acquired in October 2022 by a partnership including Mark Meisner (Birch Group) and Abe Greenhut (2020 Vision) for $346 million. The loan has been troubled since origination, with net cash flow failing to meet underwriting, though debt service has remained current due to the loan's low leverage when originated in 2016.
stories.impact: Jersey City office distress signals broader Northeast urban office weakness and rising refinance/maturity risk in the CMBS market. While this does not directly affect multifamily, it reflects depressed office values and capital constraints in the broader New Jersey/Hudson Waterfront market, which could suppress land values and slow competing development activity, indirectly benefiting multifamily projects seeking sites. Developers should monitor distressed office towers for conversion-to-residential potential or ground-floor retail repositioning that could anchor mixed-use multifamily in Jersey City.
